Description:
A sphere and a cylinder tangent to each other with a crossing intersection curve - the pair that is easy
to overlook, because the obvious sphere/cylinder tangencies do something else.
A sphere of radius 16 has its centre at (-1.9534089267, -5.6731114536, 7), that is at distance 6 from
the axis of a cylinder of radius 10 about the z axis. Because 6 + 10 = 16, the sphere touches the
cylinder at exactly one point,
  (3.2556815446, 9.4551857560, 7)
and the surfaces CROSS there: at the height of the sphere centre the two circles - the cylinder's of
radius 10 and the sphere's of radius 16 - are internally tangent, while at every other height they meet
transversally in two points, so the intersection curve has a NODE at the contact.

The curvature argument says the same thing and says when it works. The cylinder has the principal
curvatures 1/10 and 0, the sphere 1/16 in every direction, and
  1/10 - 1/16 > 0   while   0 - 1/16 < 0
is indefinite. The condition is simply sphere radius > cylinder radius, with the sphere bulging outwards
through the wall. That is the whole family: a sphere of the SAME radius as the cylinder touches it along
a circle instead, a smaller sphere tangent from inside touches in an isolated point and does not cross,
and two tangent spheres never cross at all, because the difference of two definite forms of the same
sign cannot be indefinite. A cone behaves like the cylinder here, with its local radius of curvature
taking the place of 10.

The contact is at the azimuth 71 degrees and at z = 7, so it lies in the interior of a half mantle - the
cylinder about the z axis through the origin is split in the xz plane - and far from both end faces.
This is the oblique member of the group; the seam variants are
EqualCylindersCrossedAtSeam, ConesCommonInsphereAtSeam, TorusVillarceauPlaneAtSeam,
TorusPlaneTangentInnerEquator and TorusSphereSaddleAtSeam.
Expected:
V(cylinder r=10, l=60) = 6000*pi = 18849.5559215388, area 2*pi*10*60 + 2*pi*100 = 4398.2297150257,
extent -10,-10,-30 .. 10,10,30.
V(sphere r=16) = 4/3*pi*4096 = 17157.2846788051, area 4*pi*256 = 3216.9908772759,
extent -17.9534089267,-21.6731114536,-9 .. 14.0465910733,10.3268885464,23.
The sphere spans z from -9 to 23 and is therefore nowhere near the cylinder's end faces: the contact is
the only degeneracy in the case.

The intersection is a solid of revolution problem only in the cross section, so it was integrated over z
as the area of the lens of the two circles (radius 10 at the axis and radius sqrt(256-(z-7)^2) at
distance 6), by Simpson on 400000 intervals:
  cylSphereInter      7975.6460   (Monte Carlo 7970.4 +- 3.6 with 3e6 samples, 1.4 sigma)
  cylMinusSphere      18849.5559 - 7975.6460 = 10873.9100
  sphereMinusCyl      17157.2847 - 7975.6460 =  9181.6387
  cylSphereUnion      18849.5559 + 17157.2847 - 7975.6460 = 28031.1946
The identity union + intersect = 36006.8406 is exact.

cylMinusSphere must be TWO solids. At z = 7, the height of the sphere centre, the cross section of the
sphere is a circle of radius 16 at distance 6 from the axis and therefore CONTAINS the disc of radius
10 of the cylinder, touching it at the contact point: the cylinder is cut through at that height and
the two parts, 7636.07 below and 3237.84 above, hang together at that one point alone.
sphereMinusCyl is one solid pinched at the same point, euler 1 - its annular cross section there
closes to a point. The intersection and the union are single manifold solids with euler 2. The
failures to look for are a half of cylMinusSphere going missing and a sliver face at the contact.

CORRECTION to the first version of the Expected text, which claimed all four results are single solids:
cylMinusSphere is TWO solids and that is right. At z = 7, the height of the sphere centre, the sphere's
cross section is a circle of radius 16 at distance 6 from the axis, so it CONTAINS the cylinder's disc
of radius 10 and touches it at the one contact point. The cylinder is therefore cut through at that
height and hangs together at the contact point alone - 7636.07 below it and 3237.84 above it, meeting
at z = 7 in both extents. sphereMinusCyl comes out with euler 1, pinched at the same point, and the
intersection and the union are single manifold solids with euler 2, as expected.
